reasoning_traces.think:
CQR operates by first fitting quantile regressors q̂_lo and q̂_hi at levels α/2 and 1−α/2 on a proper training set. These estimates define a prediction interval for each input x. The conformal step then computes calibration scores E_i = max(q̂_lo − y, y − q̂_hi) for each observation in the calibration set. These scores are used to adjust the interval width such that the empirical coverage matches the nominal level α. This process ensures finite-sample validity regardless of the underlying quantile estimator's consistency. In GSE, this translates to generating margin and total intervals from game feature vectors using trained quantile models, with adjustments made via conformal scores. The key insight is that while the base quantile estimator affects interval width, its correctness does not impact validity—a separation crucial for robustness in unpredictable environments like sports.
